page: Microsoft Azure M416s_v2 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the MSv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 416 dedicated vCPUs derived from 208 physical cores of Intel Xeon 8280L processors operating at 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with a massive memory footprint of 5700.0 GB, providing approximately 13.7 GB of RAM per vCPU, and includes 8389 GB of local SSD storage. It is premium storage capable but does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a significant contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. While single-core performance is relatively weak, ranking in the bottom 25% for stress-ng and Geekbench tests, the massive core count drives multi-core performance into the top 10% tier. This is demonstrated by exceptional results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Passmark CPU tests, and ray tracing. Memory bandwidth is also highly competitive, achieving top-tier status in both cached and uncached large-block read and write operations.

Given its massive memory capacity and high multi-core throughput, the M416s_v2 is highly optimized for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise relational databases, and heavy data-processing pipelines. This is supported by its top-tier Redis SET performance of 260.18 million operations per second and high static web serving throughput. However, the server exhibits poor text generation speeds in LLM inference tasks, making it less suitable for real-time generative AI workloads without dedicated GPU acceleration. It represents a high-density, consolidated resource profile for enterprise workloads requiring vast RAM and high parallel CPU capacity.
description: Microsoft Azure M416s_v2 is a high-capacity, memory-optimized server from the MSv2 family, powered by Intel Xeon 8280L processors on the x86_64 architecture. Running on Microsoft Hyper-V, it delivers 416 dedicated vCPUs across 208 physical cores, paired with an extensive 5700.0 GB of RAM and 8389 GB of local SSD storage. While single-core benchmarks rank in the bottom 25%, its multi-core and memory bandwidth performance sit in the top 10% tier. This massive parallel processing capability is reflected in exceptional multi-threaded decompression, Passmark CPU scores, and Redis SET operations exceeding 260 million operations per second. Lacking GPU acceleration, it is not suited for intensive LLM text generation but excels in hosting massive in-memory databases, enterprise database management systems, and high-throughput data warehousing workloads.
